neighbours.label: the slot where a statement's standing or validity is asserted ('are to be regarded [as standard]', 'may not be reliable'), the other side of the - pole's 'arbitrary / does not matter'
fire: The dimensions stated in metric units are to be regarded as the official ones.
These tables are widely regarded by engineers as the accepted reference.
Experts say the answer is not that simple when it comes to sleep.
Such claims are often presented in textbooks as established facts.
Readings from older sensors may not be reliable for daily monitoring.
The listed tolerances shall be considered binding for all suppliers.
Results from tiny trials are unlikely to be useful in setting policy.
The figures in the appendix are to be taken as the authoritative version.
quiet: The choice of metric units for these dimensions is entirely arbitrary.
The name you give these tables does not really matter to engineers.
Any answer will do here, since the starting point is chosen arbitrarily.
The label is simply an arbitrary number used to sort the claims.
The order of the sensors is not important for daily monitoring.
Suppliers can pick whatever colour they like; it makes no difference.
The exact cut-off for a tiny trial is somewhat arbitrary in practice.
The numbering of the figures in the appendix is a matter of convenience.

notes: Card: + pole peaks on 'are to be [regarded] as standard', 'the [answer] is not that clear', 'may not be reliable'; - pole on 'arbitrarily', 'not important', 'don't really matter'. Output promotes 'standard', 'accurate' and suppresses 'arbitrary'. Near misses are the - pole's side of that distinction.
